judgments.why: The guide states that GitHub OAuth apps can be registered instantly in developer settings with no verification required.
The guide states that you can enter up to 10 callback URLs in your app settings.
The guide does not mention error=redirect_uri_mismatch or specific error behavior for mismatched redirect URIs.
The guide mentions access token request limits but does not state that authenticated REST API requests are limited to 5,000 per hour per user.
The guide does not mention GitHub's recommendation of GitHub Apps over OAuth apps.
The guide does not mention Public Distribution for installing the app outside your own workspace.
The guide states that the redirect_uri must use HTTPS.
The guide does not mention rate limits for conversations.history based on app creation dates.
The guide does not specify the review duration of up to 10 weeks for new Marketplace submissions.
The guide does not state the requirement for the app to be installed on at least 10 active workspaces for Marketplace submission.
The guide does not mention limits on test users for apps in Testing publishing status.
The guide does not state that test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire after seven days in Testing mode.
The guide does not mention annual third-party security assessments for restricted-scope data.
The guide does not mention how long restricted scope verification takes.
The guide does not state that brand verification is required first and takes 2-3 business days.
The guide does not mention full mailbox access or gmail.readonly as restricted scopes.
The guide states that Spotify apps start in Development Mode with limits on users.
The guide does not mention that every user must be added to the app's allowlist in development mode.
The guide does not mention if the app owner needs Spotify Premium.
The guide contains no information about May 15, 2025 or extended quota rules for organizations.
The guide does not state any requirement for 250k monthly active users.
The guide explicitly states that localhost is not allowed as a redirect URI and that HTTPS or 127.0.0.1 loopback should be used.
The guide does not mention multitenant apps consent rules or risk-based step-up consent.
The guide does not discuss publisher verification or Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program accounts.
The guide only states that redirect rules must match the generated URI, without specifying https requirements or localhost exceptions.
The guide does not state whether redirect URIs are case-sensitive.
The guide does not mention tenant admin consent restrictions regarding verified publishers.
The guide does not mention app tiers or default connections.
The guide does not discuss the Core tier or connection limits related to tiers.
The guide does not mention listings on the Xero App Store or tier requirements for listing.
The guide does not mention pricing tiers like Core costing $35 AUD.
The guide does not mention app certification requirements for higher tiers.
The guide does not discuss the pricing model details of the X API beyond mentioning cost is Free/Tiered.
The guide does not mention buying credits upfront in the Developer Console.
The guide does not state whether different endpoints have different costs.
The guide does not mention business verification for advanced access.
The guide does not contain any information about Marketing API call thresholds.
The guide does not discuss the renaming of Standard Access or Advanced Access for the Marketing API.
